impact:
Discovered while fixing T-009's real-client capture, and it is a property of the CLIENT rather than of our code, so it will reach users of the v0.2 MCP server (T-013).

Measured on codex-cli 0.144.0. When `codex exec` runs without the operator's `~/.codex/config.toml` (via --ignore-user-config), a tool call to a `-c`-declared MCP server is CANCELLED BY THE CLIENT before the request is ever sent:

  client -> server : initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/list        (and nothing more)
  server -> client : correct initialize result, correct tools/list result
  client stderr    : mcp: spendbar-probe/spendbar_probe started
                     mcp: spendbar-probe/spendbar_probe (failed)
                     user cancelled MCP tool call
  client stdout    : "The MCP tool call was canceled and did not succeed."

The server is blameless — it answered both requests correctly and never received tools/call.

The governing setting is per-server: `mcp_servers.<name>.default_tools_approval_mode`, whose accepted values are `auto`, `prompt`, `writes`, `approve`. The default (`auto`) cancels in a non-interactive `codex exec` run with no prior approval on record. `approve` fixes it.

What did NOT fix it, each measured rather than assumed: a `projects."<cwd>".trust_level="trusted"` override for the run's scratch cwd; dropping `--ephemeral`. What DID also work and was rejected: `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, which disables the sandbox for everything the model might run in order to solve one server's tool approval.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE SPIKE. A user who adds spendbar's MCP server to Codex and drives it non-interactively can see their tool calls cancelled with an error that names spendbar and looks like our server failed ("(failed)"), when nothing on our side went wrong. T-013 should decide what to do about it: at minimum document the required approval setting in the Codex setup instructions, and consider whether the registration snippet we tell users to paste should include `default_tools_approval_mode`.

Also worth recording as evidence hygiene: the previous Codex captures in this repo passed only because the operator's own config.toml had entries that approved the call. That is precisely the contamination ISS-047 was filed about, now demonstrated rather than suspected — isolating the config is what made the requirement visible at all.
title: Codex cancels an MCP tool call unless the server is approved in config — affects how spendbar's MCP server is documented for Codex users
